transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’ve just been a little off lately. Ever since a friend from my choir passed away so suddenly, I haven’t quite been myself. I know people go through these things, and I don’t want to make too much of it, but I find myself crying over silly things, like the potluck lists, and getting all worked up over phone calls I used to handle just fine. I’ve even missed a couple of church planning things, which isn’t like me at all. Is that… the sort of thing you mean?
Have you found that things you usually enjoy, like choir or church events, don’t interest you as much anymore?

I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost interest, exactly. I still care about choir and the church things… I suppose I just haven’t felt quite as eager to go sometimes. But once I’m there, I do try to participate. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of choir or church events as you used to, even when you do go?

I’m not sure… I wouldn’t want to say I don’t enjoy them. I still like seeing people and hearing the music. Maybe it feels a little flatter than it used to, but I do still get something out of it when I’m there. Is that answering what you mean?
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day, nearly every day… that sounds a little strong, maybe. But since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I really haven’t felt like myself. I cry over things that shouldn’t set me off, like potluck lists, and I get all worked up over calls I used to handle just fine. And I’ve missed some church planning things I never would’ve missed before. So… yes, something’s been weighing on me, I suppose.
Would you say that most days, for most of the day, your mood has been down or sad since your friend passed away?

Most days… yes, I think my mood has been lower than usual. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I cry over little things, like those potluck lists, and I get worked up about calls I used to handle easily. I’ve even missed some church planning things I normally never would’ve missed. So… I suppose sad or down is fair to say.
Would you say that your sadness or low mood is present for most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?

I think… yes, it’s been there most days. I don’t want to overstate it, but ever since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I cry over things like the potluck lists, and calls I used to handle easily get me all worked up. And I’ve started missing church planning things I really never would’ve missed before. So I guess the low mood is there a lot, yes.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, no longer give you the same sense of pleasure or satisfaction they used to?

I’m not sure I’d say they give me no pleasure anymore. I mean, I still care about choir and church things… they’ve always meant a lot to me. Maybe it doesn’t feel quite the same right now, but I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it. I suppose I’m having a harder time getting the usual satisfaction from it, but I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve stopped caring.
Would you say that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like choir or church events, even when you do them?

I don’t think I’d say I no longer take pleasure in them, exactly. That sounds a bit stronger than what I mean. I still do care about choir and church things, and sometimes it’s still nice to be there. It’s just… maybe it doesn’t feel as easy or as full as it used to. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in choir or church events, or that you no longer care about them the way you used to?

Completely lost interest? No, I don’t think that’s right. I’d feel bad saying that, because I do still care about choir and the church events. They’re important to me. It’s just… I may not feel as lively about them right now, or it takes more effort, but I haven’t stopped caring. Is that distinction okay?
Would you say that being in the choir or attending church events feels like a chore now, or that you don’t get any joy from them at all, even when you’re there?

I wouldn’t call it a chore, no… at least not exactly. And I don’t think it’s true that I get no joy from it at all. When I’m there, there are still moments that feel nice or comforting. Maybe I’m not as uplifted as I used to be, but I don’t want to overstate it. I still care about being part of it. Is that answering what you mean?
Would you say that you take less pleasure or interest in choir or church events than you used to, even when you're there?

I’m… not sure how to put it exactly. Maybe a little less, yes, but I don’t want to make it sound like I don’t enjoy them or don’t care. I still do. It’s just maybe not quite the same feeling as before, or it takes me a bit more to get into it. Is that fair to say?
Would you say that you’ve lost pleasure in almost all activities, not just choir or church events?

I don’t think I’d say almost all activities, no. I mean… I have off moments, but I haven’t really noticed that everything feels joyless or anything like that. Maybe I’m a bit less enthusiastic sometimes, but “lost pleasure in almost all activities” sounds stronger than what I’d want to say. Is that okay?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, not just choir or church events?

I don’t think I’d say most things, no. I mean, I have days where I’m not as eager or it takes me a little more to get going, but I still can enjoy things once I’m doing them. So… maybe some things feel a bit dulled, but “lost interest or pleasure in most things” sounds like more than I’m experiencing. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of pleasure or interest in most of your usual activities, not just choir or church events, nearly every day over the past two weeks?

I don’t think I could say nearly every day, no. I mean, I have noticed feeling a little less interested at times, but not in most of my usual activities and not day after day like that. I still do get some enjoyment out of things. I hope that’s answering it the right way.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling a lack of energy or feeling fatigued nearly every day over the past couple of weeks?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day. I do get tired sometimes, but… I guess I’ve been thinking that’s just normal or part of getting older, you know? It hasn’t stood out to me as constant fatigue. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that you've had trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions nearly every day over the past couple of weeks?

I don’t think so… not nearly every day. I mean, I have moments where I’m distracted or I walk into a room and forget what I meant to do, but I sort of figured that happens to everybody. I wouldn’t say I’m having real trouble making decisions or thinking clearly most days. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in most of your usual activities, not just choir or church events, nearly every day over the past two weeks?

I guess… no, I wouldn’t say most of my usual activities nearly every day. There are times I’m not as enthusiastic as I used to be, but I still find some pleasure in things. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you’ve felt a noticeable loss of pleasure or interest in most of the things you used to enjoy, not just choir or church events, over the past two weeks?

I don’t think I’d say most things, no. I mean, maybe I’m a little less excited about some things lately, but I still can enjoy myself here and there. So… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that an okay way to put it?
